entry.title: ARC-Impute: robust reference-guided spatial gene imputation through regularised cell-to-spot mapping
entry.summary:
Motivation: Reference-guided spatial imputation uses single-cell RNA sequencing references to predict genes that are unmeasured in spatial transcriptomics data. Limited shared-gene overlap can leave the mapping of reference cells to spatial locations ambiguous: different assignments may reconstruct observed genes similarly yet yield different imputed expression and cell-type estimates. This gives rise to local assignment ambiguity, source-target mismatch and reference-transfer instability.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: MitoArc: A Reproducible Short-Read Workflow for Human Mitochondrial Genome Analysis with Circular-Coordinate and NUMT-Aware Evaluation
entry.summary:
Human mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) analysis from short-read sequencing is complicated by nuclear mitochondrial DNA segments (NUMTs), circular-reference coordinates, sequencing depth, and variant-caller configuration. We developed MitoArc, a Nextflow workflow that accepts paired-end FASTQ files or pre-aligned BAM and CRAM files, retains available nuclear mapping context, and performs standard and shifted-coordinate processing. It runs Genome Analysis Toolkit (GATK) Mutect2 and mutserve2 independently and reports mitochondrial quality metrics, NUMT evidence, haplogroups, contamination estimates, functional annotations, consensus sequences, and reproducibility outputs.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #consensus
